theme: 3 terms on writing tricky text in code: special characters with a backslash, strings over many lines, and strings that keep every backslash as typed

terms.definition: A backslash followed by a letter or symbol that puts a special character, like a new line or a quote, into a string.
terms.example: Add a new line Escape Sequence instead of calling `print` twice.
terms.code:
print("She said \"Ship it\"")
print("Line one\nLine two")
terms.output:
She said "Ship it"
Line one
Line two

terms.definition: A string that starts and ends with three quotes, so it can run over several lines.
terms.example: Put the email template in a Multiline String Literal, it's much easier to edit.
terms.code:
let note = """
    Release 2.0
    - Dark mode
    """
print(note)

terms.definition: A string wrapped in hash signs, where backslashes and quotes are kept exactly as typed.
terms.example: Write the file path as a Raw String, so you don't double every backslash.
terms.code:
let path = #"C:\Users\mina"#
print(path)
let n = 3
print(#"Count: \#(n)"#)

quizzes.question: In this code, what do you call the string wrapped in hash signs?
What do you call a backslash plus a letter that puts a special character, like a new line, into a string?
What do you call a string that opens and closes with three quotes and can run over many lines?

video.description:
Learn to explain string syntax in Swift: Escape Sequence, Multiline String Literal & Raw String, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Escape Sequence - A backslash followed by a letter or symbol that puts a special character, like a new line or a quote, into a string.
Multiline String Literal - A string that starts and ends with three quotes, so it can run over several lines.
Raw String - A string wrapped in hash signs, where backslashes and quotes are kept exactly as typed.

landscape.description:
Explain Escape Sequence, Multiline String Literal & Raw String in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
이스케이프 시퀀스, 여러 줄 문자열 리터럴, 원시 문자열 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Escape Sequence - A backslash followed by a letter or symbol that puts a special character, like a new line or a quote, into a string.
한국어: 이스케이프 시퀀스: 백슬래시 뒤에 글자나 기호를 붙여 줄바꿈이나 따옴표 같은 특수 문자를 문자열에 넣는 방법

Multiline String Literal - A string that starts and ends with three quotes, so it can run over several lines.
한국어: 여러 줄 문자열 리터럴: 따옴표 세 개로 시작하고 끝나서 여러 줄에 걸쳐 쓸 수 있는 문자열

Raw String - A string wrapped in hash signs, where backslashes and quotes are kept exactly as typed.
한국어: 원시 문자열: 해시 기호로 감싸서 백슬래시와 따옴표를 입력한 그대로 유지하는 문자열

landscape.hook: Can you explain Swift string literals in English?

dialogue.title: Too many backslashes

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my test JSON in `old` is full of backslashes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's an Escape Sequence. It puts a quote inside the string.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It works, but I can't read it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Try a Raw String, like `json`. With hash signs, quotes need no escaping.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So in a Raw String, a backslash is just a backslash?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. An Escape Sequence there needs a hash after the backslash.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nice. But the real response has ten fields.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then use a Multiline String Literal, like `body`. Three quotes open and close it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They stay as typed. A Multiline String Literal doesn't need escapes for them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Hash signs for short JSON, three quotes for long.

dialogue.code:
let old = "{\"name\": \"Mina\"}"
let json = #"{"name": "Mina"}"#
let body = """
    {"name": "Mina", "team": "iOS"}
    """

lines.text: An Escape Sequence lets you put a quote inside a string.
